elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered text opens "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ... EXCEED", replacing the one-sided "TRUELINK'S LIABILITY"; the carve-out is likewise recast as "A PARTY'S", so the cap and its exceptions run both ways.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Retained basis is "THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD": no USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid" only (not "paid or payable"), a narrowed hosting/support subset rather than all fees, and the 12-month window is not anchored to the event giving rise to the claim.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The rendered sentence contains no exclusion of indirect, consequential, special or incidental damages for either party; only a monetary cap is stated.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Parenthetical excepts "A PARTY'S ... BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS" from the cap, so confidentiality breaches sit outside the ceiling for both parties.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list is limited to indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out was added.
Parenthetical excepts "A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS", which places the Section 12(a) Client indemnity and any Vendor indemnity outside the cap.
"OTHER THAN A PARTY'S ... GROSS NEGLIGENCE" — the original TrueLink-only gross negligence exception is now mutual.
"OTHER THAN A PARTY'S ... WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" appears in the carve-out parenthetical and applies to either party.
No fraud carve-out appears in the rendered parenthetical.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out appears; only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are excepted.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing states that Client's obligation to pay compensation/fees is not "damages" for cap purposes; the rendered clause is silent.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ... EXCEED ..." — the cap now protects Client as well as TrueLink, curing the walk-away one-sidedness.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Retained verbatim: "THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — a 12-month fee basis tied to the compensation for the contracted hosting and support services (not an illusory set-up fee).
Carve-out expressly names "A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS" as outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out expressly names "BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS" (Section 10 obligations) as outside the cap.
"OTHER THAN A PARTY'S ... GROSS NEGLIGENCE" — mutual exception retained and extended to both parties.
"OTHER THAN A PARTY'S ... WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" — mutual exception in the operative parenthetical.

reasons: Finding status is correct: the original p0077 caps only TrueLink while leaving Client (including the broad Section 12(a) indemnity) uncapped, which is walk-away territory, so the clause fails the fallback and a redline is warranted.

The fallback checklist is complete on the rendered language: mutual aggregate cap, retained 12-month fee basis, and mutual carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. The proposal is therefore position-complete at the fallback level.

Preferred level is not reached: no USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid" rather than "paid or payable", the 12-month window is not anchored to the event giving rise to the claim, and there is no mutual indirect/consequential exclusion and no carve-out for data protection/security, fraud or IP infringement, and no statement that Client's payment obligations are not "damages".

Minimality fails: the redline deletes the scope words "SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11", converting a cap that previously reached only four sections into an agreement-wide cap. That deletion is not required by any fallback element (mutuality is achieved solely by "TRUELINK'S" -> "EITHER PARTY'S"), and it strips a Customer-favourable restriction by extending TrueLink's cap protection to matters (e.g. warranty and service-performance breaches) where TrueLink was previously uncapped. Repair by keeping the section scope, i.e. "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 OF THIS AGREEMENT ...", or expressly justify the broadening as necessary to cap Client's exposure outside those sections.

Intent is preserved in the strict sense: no defined term is left undefined, no cross-reference dangles, and the fee basis, carve-out structure and the surrounding indemnity mechanics survive without contradiction (the previously TrueLink-only gross negligence/wilful misconduct exception is retained and made mutual).

Note for the drafter: if the Agreement charges compensation other than for hosting and support (e.g. transaction, licence or set-up fees), the retained basis may understate 12 months' fees; consider "total compensation paid or payable by Client under this Agreement" when the clause is reopened, together with the USD 1,000,000 floor and the payment-obligation carve-out flagged in the comment.
